Bayesian Dirichlet-Multinomial comparison of two transition networks

Source: R/bayes_compare.R
bayes_compare.Rd

bayes_compare() compares two transition networks edge by edge and returns, for every transition, the posterior mean difference in transition probability, a credible interval, and the probability that the difference lies on its side of zero. The transitions out of each state are modelled as a multinomial draw with a Dirichlet prior on the transition probabilities, so the posterior for the transitions out of state \(i\) is \(\mathrm{Dirichlet}(c_i + \alpha)\), where \(c_i\) are the observed outgoing counts and \(\alpha\) is prior. Each edge probability is then marginally Beta-distributed: the posterior mean difference has a closed form, and the credible interval comes from Monte Carlo draws. It takes two networks estimated by build_network() with method "relative" or "frequency" (for either, the difference is in transition probabilities estimated from the counts), a group of networks, or two edge-betweenness networks from net_edge_betweenness() (see Details). An mcml object raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input: its layers hold different states and carry no transition counts.

The comparison complements permutation(): the permutation test asks whether a difference is more extreme than chance, and this comparison gives the plausible range of the difference and how precisely the counts estimate it. An edge whose source state has few outgoing transitions gets a wide interval even when its row-normalised probabilities look far apart. An edge is flagged as credibly different when its interval excludes zero and its mean and nearest bound pass mean_threshold and bound_threshold; the thresholds are conventions, and no correction is made for comparing many edges at once. The reported p_value (the Bayesian p-equivalent \(2(1 - p_d)\), with \(p_d\) the probability of direction) summarises posterior mass and is not a frequentist p-value. The model treats every transition as an independent draw, so it does not account for transitions being nested in sequences, which a permutation of sequences with permutation() respects.

Usage

bayes_compare(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  prior = 0.5,
  draws = 10000L,
  ci = 0.95,
  mean_threshold = 0.01,
  bound_threshold = 0.001,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'net_bayes'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_bayes'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_bayes'
plot(x, significant_only = TRUE, title = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_bayes_group'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_bayes_group'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

x

The first network: a netobject estimated with "relative" or "frequency" or one of their aliases, a netobject_group, or a net_edge_betweenness object. A bare cograph_network is recounted from the sequences it carries, and used only when they reproduce its weights; otherwise, and for an mcml, an error of class nestimate_bad_input is raised. Both networks must use the same method and hold the same nodes; any other method raises an error, because the model needs transition counts. For the print() and plot() methods: a net_bayes, or for print() a net_bayes_group.

y

The second network, of the same kind as x. Default NULL: with a netobject_group as x, every pair of its groups is compared. With two netobject_groups, the groups sharing a name are compared, and an error is raised when none do.

prior

The Dirichlet concentration added to every cell of the count matrices, a positive number. Default 0.5, the Jeffreys prior; 1 gives a uniform (Laplace) prior. Every cell gets it, so a transition observed in neither network still has a small posterior probability.

draws

The number of Monte Carlo posterior draws behind the credible intervals, at least 2. Default 10000. For edge-betweenness networks the betweenness is recomputed on every draw, so time grows with draws.

ci

The mass of the equal-tailed credible interval, a number between 0 and 1. Default 0.95.

mean_threshold

The absolute posterior mean difference an edge must exceed to be flagged as credibly different. Default 0.01, on the transition-probability scale.

bound_threshold

The absolute value the interval bound nearest zero must exceed for an edge to be flagged. It guards against differences that are detectable but negligibly small. Default 0.001.

seed

An integer that makes the draws reproducible; the session's own random stream is left as it was. Default NULL. For a group, it is set again before each comparison.

...

For plot(): further arguments for cograph::splot() when cograph is installed (such as weight_digits, the digits the drawn differences are rounded to, default 2, or edge_label_digits, the digits of the edge labels, default 3); otherwise ignored. The print() and summary() methods ignore it.

object

For summary(): a net_bayes or net_bayes_group.

significant_only

For plot(): whether to draw only the edges flagged as credibly different. Default TRUE. When no edge is left to draw, an error suggests significant_only = FALSE.

title

For plot(): the plot title. Default NULL, which gives "Bayesian network difference" (with cograph) or a title naming the posterior mean difference (without it).

Value

A net_bayes object (class c("net_bayes", "netdifference", "net_permutation")), or, for a netobject_group input, a net_bayes_group: a list of net_bayes objects named by comparison ("A vs B"), or by group name when two groups are compared. print() shows the method, the prior, draws, interval and thresholds, and the numbers of nodes, of edges compared and of edges credibly different (for a group, it lists the comparisons); summary() returns one row per edge observed in at least one network (for a group, with a comparison column); and plot() draws the difference network. A net_bayes carries the same fields as a permutation() result, so it is accepted wherever a net_permutation is, and also carries a difference matrix for the netdifference verbs (as_netdifference(), cograph's difference plots). Its fields:

x, y

The two input networks.

diff

Posterior mean difference matrix (prob_x - prob_y); the analogue of the permutation test's observed difference.

difference_matrix

The same matrix as diff, for cograph's netdifference helpers.

diff_sig

The difference where sig is TRUE, else 0.

p_values

The two-sided Bayesian p-equivalent, in the field a net_permutation consumer reads as p-values (see p_bayes).

effect_size

Posterior mean difference over its posterior standard deviation (0 where that is 0).

ci_lower, ci_upper

Credible-interval bound matrices.

p_difference

Probability of direction: the share of posterior mass on the dominant side of zero, in \([0.5, 1]\).

p_bayes

The same matrix as p_values: the two-sided Bayesian p-equivalent \(2(1-\mathrm{p\_difference})\). It summarises posterior mass, not a frequentist tail probability, so it is not a p-value and should not be reported as one.

prob_x, prob_y

Posterior mean transition-probability matrices (posterior mean betweenness for edge-betweenness input).

sig

Logical matrix: the interval excludes zero and the mean and nearest bound exceed their thresholds.

summary

The per-edge table that summary() returns, with the columns of a net_permutation summary (from, to, weight_x, weight_y, diff, effect_size, p_value, sig) plus count_x, count_y, ci_lower, ci_upper, ci_width and p_difference.

method, iter, alpha, paired, adjust

Permutation-compatible settings (iter = draws, alpha = 1 - ci, paired = FALSE, adjust = "none"); method is "edge_betweenness" for edge-betweenness input.

prior, draws, ci, mean_threshold, bound_threshold

The Bayesian settings.

observed_diff, source_method, edge_betweenness

For edge-betweenness input only: the plug-in difference, the source networks' method and the betweenness settings.

For the print() methods: the input, invisibly. For summary(): the per-edge data frame described under the summary field; for a net_bayes_group, the tables of every comparison stacked, with a comparison column first. For plot(): with cograph installed, it draws the difference network with cograph::splot(), each edge labelled with its posterior mean difference and credible interval, and returns the cograph_network invisibly; without cograph, it returns a ggplot chord diagram in which colour gives the direction of the difference and width its size.

Details

For two net_edge_betweenness objects (source method "relative" only), edge betweenness is a nonlinear function of the whole transition matrix, so Beta marginals do not apply. Instead the full transition matrix is drawn from each network's row-wise Dirichlet posterior and edge betweenness is recomputed on every draw, the Bayesian analogue of permutation() on edge-betweenness networks. The result summarises the posterior of \(EB(x) - EB(y)\): diff is the posterior mean difference, prob_x and prob_y the posterior mean betweenness matrices, and observed_diff the plug-in difference of the two input networks. Both inputs must use the same invert setting, and mean_threshold and bound_threshold are then on the betweenness scale.

References

Johnston, L. & Jendoubi, T. (2026). How Delivery Mode Reshapes Resource Engagement: A Bayesian Differential Network Analysis. TNA Workshop 2026.

Gelman, A., Carlin, J. B., Stern, H. S., Dunson, D. B., Vehtari, A., & Rubin, D. B. (2013). Bayesian Data Analysis (3rd ed.). CRC Press.

Jeffreys, H. (1946). An invariant form for the prior probability in estimation problems. Proceedings of the Royal Society of London A, 186(1007), 453-461.

See also

permutation for the frequentist complement; certainty for single-network posterior edge intervals; subtract_networks and as_netdifference for the difference verbs; build_network

Examples

s1 <- data.frame(V1 = c("A","B","C"), V2 = c("B","C","A"))
s2 <- data.frame(V1 = c("A","C","B"), V2 = c("C","B","A"))
n1 <- build_network(s1, method = "relative")
n2 <- build_network(s2, method = "relative")
bayes_compare(n1, n2, draws = 500, seed = 1)
#> Bayesian Dirichlet-Multinomial Comparison: Transition Network (relative probabilities) 
#>   Prior: Dirichlet(0.50)  |  Draws: 500  |  CI: 95%
#>   Thresholds: |mean diff| > 0.010, nearest CI bound > 0.001
#>   Nodes: 3  |  Edges compared: 6  |  Credibly different: 0
